name: Differential Infrared Thermography (DIT)
definition: A technique to measure the local attenuation coefficient of a transmissive target by comparing measurements with two different radiating backgrounds, assuming the target's temperature/radiance remains constant between measurements.
summary: Differential Infrared Thermography estimates spray transmittance by comparing two IR images with different backgrounds, providing apparent temperature and optical depth without resolving internal line-of-sight distributions.
